attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post, stated in his voice.

semantics.note: Keeps his weaker 'a lot of the problem' and the 'I believe' qualifier on OpenAI. The causal element is about a present state, not a forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair: AI failures materially contributed to poor use, with no majority share required. Keeping hardware and network failures separate is reasonable.

evidence.note: Launch review from April 11. Reports mixed answer accuracy and specific wrong answers, plus non-AI problems.
Launch review from April 11. Reports frequent failures. Humane cites model hallucinations among the causes, alongside server issues.
Reports hallucinations and confused answers but also successes. Humane blames some failures on server bugs and connectivity. This does not show the AI made no material contribution.
Humane disclosure from Nov 2023 confirming an OpenAI partnership. Background for the qualified provider attribution.

reviews.rationale: Independent launch reviews show poor practical performance and recurring wrong or unreliable AI answers that materially contributed to it. Inverse shows some failures came from servers and connectivity, but not that AI problems were immaterial. Humane's disclosure backs the hedged OpenAI attribution. The support condition is met.

attribution.note: Marcus restates, in his own post and as his own view, what he told the Times.

semantics.note: A firm, universal observation about every company's technology as of the post date.

contract.note: The plain reading (dependable answers to varied everyday questions, without needing perfection) is ordinary and fair. The universal scope comes from the speaker's own words.

evidence.note: Shows one product was unreliable in April 2024. One company cannot settle a claim about every company.
March 2024 test of models via APIs on election questions only. Outside the target window, a narrow domain, and not the deployed assistants.

reviews.rationale: The packet has one product review and a narrow March API test of election questions. Neither gives broad, period-matched evidence across providers that would establish or refute the universal claim about general-purpose assistants.

attribution.note: The observation 'so far it hasn't' is Marcus's own. His paraphrase of Yudkowsky is not scored.

semantics.note: A retrospective observation limited by 'so far' to the post date.

contract.note: Living humans on April 15, 2024 settle the claim. The contract correctly leaves the Yudkowsky paraphrase unscored.

evidence.note: Same-day race report documenting living humans running the Boston Marathon on April 15, 2024.

reviews.rationale: A dated report shows humans alive and competing on April 15, 2024, so AI had not killed humanity by then.

attribution.note: Marcus's own summary judgement in his post.

semantics.note: A retrospective evaluative summary. The set of 'grand pronouncements' and what would count as 'borne out' are undefined.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no non-arbitrary way to aggregate the pronouncements. Picking particular ones would create a new claim.

evidence.note: Khan Academy's own account of Khan's 2023 talk: aspirations plus a live demo. It shows what was said, not whether it came true.

reviews.rationale: The claim is a vague aggregate judgement with no defined list of pronouncements and no success criteria, so it cannot be scored as written.
